title: From Flash games to platform work

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine didn't start in Kubernetes. He started in browser tabs, game loops, and a makerspace that smelled like hot PLA.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a better origin story than most. How far back does it go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Around 2010, in high school, building small browser games in Flash and learning HTML and JavaScript. The habit was to ship something playable, then fix what feels wrong. Years later he packaged some of that nostalgia as a Flash games site and a Docker setup for classic consoles.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Around 2015, a portfolio of game projects redone in Unity, CryEngine and Unreal. It taught him scope. By 2017 he was managing a makerspace at a college, with 3D printers and VR gear, and he built a WiFi-controlled RC car. That's also when he got serious about web development.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where does the career part start?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 2018, a five-week internship at Algolux, in computational imaging. Python tools, RAW color analysis, capture workflows. It trained a loop he still uses: measure, automate, document.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: At ÉTS, a capstone hovercraft, a hydroglisseur, with a lift fan and 3D-printed parts. A bachelor's from 2018 to 2023, helping run the AlgoÉTS algorithmic trading club. Co-ops from 2019 to 2022 at Wandrian, Power Go and Intact, then full time in 2023 at IONODES on an IoT platform. And a master's from 2023 to 2026 on real-time rendering and surface wear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The problems moved up a layer. GitLab CI/CD, GCP, Java microservices, and DevSecOps labs at Polytechnique Montréal, with GitLab templates for about twenty teams. Plus teaching at ÉTS.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He used to count features shipped. Now he cares whether a system stays understandable when he's not in the room. Reliability is trust, and security is habits in the pipeline, not a final gate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Follow problems where you see the whole loop: code, deploy, operate, improve. His started with Flash and a hovercraft. The full write-up has the timeline diagram and project links.
